topic: an academic treatment of the history and lore of ginger, the health and medical research and the ecological, botanical and molecular level research about the plant itself
question: What is known about ginger (Zingiber officinale) across its documented history and lore, the human health evidence, and the plant's own biology, and where do those three records support, complicate or contradict each other?

in: History and lore, worldwide record: origin and dispersal; ginger in the Indian, Chinese, Greco-Roman, Islamic and European medical and culinary record; the Caribbean and the Americas; folklore where a scholarly source documents it
Health, human evidence first: clinical trials, meta-analyses and umbrella reviews, the EU herbal monograph, safety and interactions, pharmacokinetics; mechanisms where they bear on humans
The plant: botany, origin and sterility, genome, gingerol biosynthesis, what the compounds do for the plant, ecology and diseases, and a short section on growing conditions relevant to a greenhouse
Kitchen chemistry as the bridge to the recipes: what drying and heating do to the pungent compounds
Recipes from dated historical sources, each cited, cross-referenced to the science
out: Cell-culture and animal findings as subjects in their own right (they appear only where labelled as such)
Present-day ethnobotanical surveys of living folk practice
Other ginger-family plants as subjects (turmeric, galangal, cardamom appear for comparison only)
The supplement industry: products, brands, extraction technology, markets
The drug-discovery pipeline: synthetic analogues, nano-formulations, patents
Commercial agronomy: yield, fertiliser, breeding, post-harvest trade
Modern recipes, the greenhouse's own Tea Time preparations, and any dose or health claim of the builder's own
boundary.rationale: Daniel wants one scholarly reference that joins the three strands his team agreed on, at a size completable inside the three-month Tea Time project.
